name: Zoan
overview: Zoan, also known as Tanis, was a significant city in Egypt built seven years after Hebron in the land of Canaan, highlighting its historical importance (Numbers 13:22). Scripture portrays the princes and wise men of Zoan, who served as counselors to Pharaoh, in a critical light, describing them as foolish and their counsel as ineffective (Isaiah 19:11, 13). This city was a center of political power and influence, with its princes and ambassadors playing key roles in Egypt's governance and diplomatic relations (Isaiah 30:4; Ezekiel 30:14). The biblical narrative underscores God's judgment upon Zoan, emphasizing His sovereign authority over even the most powerful seats of earthly wisdom and rule.
